fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "…My loving devotion promised to David." (Isaiah 55:3). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). That's a promise with a long history behind it, and God is putting it in front of everybody here.

Good name, friend, and Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), matters a lot in the Bible. But this verse names someone else. The LORD says, "…My loving devotion promised to David." (Isaiah 55:3). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3).

I see why you went there, baker. Abraham is the man God promised a great nation (Genesis 12:2). But in this verse the LORD names someone else: "…My loving devotion promised to David." (Isaiah 55:3). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3).

Careful, friend, this one went the other way. The LORD says, "…nations who do not know you will run to you." (Isaiah 55:5). Nobody is turning away. They're RUNNING toward you. It's like a crowd sprinting to the bakery when the cookies come out, except this one is nations.
Not quite, baker. The verse says, "…for He will freely pardon." (Isaiah 55:7). Freely is the word. It's a pardon that's offered with open hands.

I get the slip, baker, but the LORD says the opposite. He declares, "…My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways…" (Isaiah 55:8). His are not the same as ours. I've been wrong about a recipe before, and the LORD says His ways are higher than ours, as the heavens are higher than the earth (Isaiah 55:9).

That's a good picture, baker, but it's not what the verse says. The LORD says, "the mountains and hills will burst into song before you…" (Isaiah 55:12). No bowing here. The mountains sing. I'd pay good money to hear a mountain hit a high note.

That one sounds dramatic, friend, but it's not in this verse. The LORD says, "the mountains and hills will burst into song before you…" (Isaiah 55:12). Nothing melts. The hills are the choir, and they sing while you go out with joy. I want a front-row seat.
